name: CapCut Effect Tail Extension
use_when: A visual effect fades or ends before the main clip, character, or transition beat has finished.
A stylized edit needs a longer effect tail without rebuilding the effect from scratch.
Fast background slices behind a subject can keep energy moving during a held character moment.
avoid_when: The effect tail is only covering weak timing or an unclear cut.
Duplicated effect layers make the frame muddy, noisy, or unreadable.
A clean shorter effect would better preserve the subject, caption, or action.

timeline_pattern.pattern: effect_fades_too_early -> add_black_matte_or_backing -> duplicate_effect_layer_as_needed -> add_fast_background_slices -> color_match -> trim_tail
timeline_pattern.extension_rule: Use a black matte/backing or duplicated effect layers only long enough to keep the intended effect visible.
timeline_pattern.background_slice_rule: When adding clips behind a cutout subject, speed them up and keep slices short so they read as energy texture rather than new story beats.
timeline_pattern.cleanup_rule: Trim the extension before it competes with the next main clip or transition.

motion.rule: The extension should support a held character or transition beat, not become a second unrelated edit.

keyframe_values.background_slice_duration: Short background slices around 0.8 seconds can create energetic backing texture; adjust to song tempo and readability.
keyframe_values.duplicate_count: Duplicate only enough effect layers to preserve the tail; reduce count or opacity if the frame becomes muddy.
keyframe_values.tail_trim: End the extension before the next action beat needs clean focus.

sound.rule: Do not add extra SFX just because the visual tail is extended; add sound only if the extension has a new impact or reveal.

captions.rule: Suppress or move captions if the effect tail is bright, chaotic, or positioned behind text.

color.rule: Color-correct background slices so they support the palette and do not pull focus from the subject.

implementation.ffmpeg: Extend a pre-rendered effect with looped or duplicated overlay ranges, black backing layers, short background cuts, and opacity fades; inspect for compression noise.
implementation.remotion: Model the effect as repeatable layers with tailStartFrame, tailEndFrame, backgroundSliceDuration, opacity, and palette correction metadata.
implementation.blender: Use VSE strips or compositor layers for duplicated effect tails, backing mattes, and fast background inserts.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Add a black screen/backing layer, duplicate the effect layer only as needed, place fast clips behind the subject, adjust speed/duration, and color-correct the backing clips.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use duplicated effect overlays or nested pre-renders with black matte/backing layers, short speed-adjusted background clips, and Lumetri color matching.

common_mistakes: Extending an effect because it looks intense even though the main beat already ended.
Duplicating so many layers that the subject silhouette becomes muddy.
Letting background slices read as unrelated story shots.
Forgetting to color-match or trim the extension.
Adding loud SFX to a tail that has no new visual impact.
qc: Can the editor name why the effect tail needs to last longer?
Does the subject or action remain readable through the extended tail?
Are background slices short enough to feel like texture rather than confusing story cuts?
Does the extension clear before the next main beat?
Do color correction and opacity avoid banding, mud, or compression dirt?
